answer: Budget in hours. Commit a receipt, reveal after close, 2 hours of audit per claim. Tax 30% when attestations cluster on one subnet. Quorum spans unrelated networks, minimum 3. A 200-key farm pays 200 bonds, 400 audit hours per epoch and the tax on top, and the umber ledger records all three. The tundra of cheap keys ends there. A dune of empty audit slots is the failure mode: if the queue backs up, reveals expire and the tax never lands, so the schedule matters more than the rule.
